transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Verdant Head of Alliances), Carlos Mendez (Verdant Sales), Lena Zhao (Verdant Solutions Architect), Tom Redding (Verdant VP)

Auto-generated summary: (may be noisy)
- Partners: discuss co-sell pipeline, pilot, bench marks, exec alignment

[00:00] Elena Park: Alright, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Elena from Redwood here, happy to kick off. Marcus is on the line for the technical bits.
[00:12] Priya Kaur: Hey Elena, thanks. Quick schedule sync, we have Tom on for the first 15, he needs to drop at 30 if that's okay.
[00:20] Tom Redding: yep, short window, i just want to make sure the exec asks are clear.
[00:28] Elena Park: Totally. Today we want to 1) agree on which accounts to prioritize for joint outreach, 2) define a minimal pilot and success metrics, 3) plan technical bench timing and 4) commercial handoff.
[00:43] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. From Verdant's side we've got a mix of net-new logos and a few refresh opportunities with existing customers.
[00:52] Marcus Li: Quick note on the bench, we'll need a representative prompt set and sample token distributions — sequence lengths, percent of long-form, that sort of thing. Also access pattern: are these chat flows or single-turn generation?
[01:10] Lena Zhao: Mostly multi-turn chat but with long context for some accounts, like up to 8k tokens. Also some embedding workloads for search.
[01:21] Marcus Li: Great — that helps with which model family we suggest and whether we advise quant or full fp16.
[01:28] Tom Redding: On the commercial front, we care about clear crediting and rep coverage. Verdant wants to own the account when we bring introductions, but share upside from licence and usage.
[01:42] Elena Park: Understood. We usually do a co-sell revenue share or referral fee + inbound lead ownership. We can bake in a joint-account plan for the pilot.
[01:52] Priya Kaur: Can we carve out some SLAs? Our enterprise customers will ask.
[01:57] Elena Park: Yes, for Dedicated we can include SLA language. For hosted we have standard uptime S-L-A info — apologies i always say es el ay —. We'll share the doc.
[02:08] Carlos Mendez: One hesitation i have — cost. For certain deals, latency at scale is non-negotiable but customers balk at price. How do you typically balance that?
[02:18] Marcus Li: We suggest a hybrid routing approach: low-latency paths for latency-sensitive endpoints and cheaper model variants for bulk async workloads. Also prefix caching — or kayvee cash as my kid says — can cut token costs for repeated starts.
[02:33] Elena Park: We'll provide model recommendations per account — per your use case we can propose dedicated capacity for the high-throughput ones and hosted for lower-volume.
[02:42] Lena Zhao: For security/regulatory accounts, what's your private deployment story? We might need on-prem or VPC with KMS/HSM integration.
[02:51] Marcus Li: We support Private deploy with customer-managed VPC and KMS. There is a setup window but it's common for finance and healthcare. We do audit logs and RBAC too.
[03:03] Priya Kaur: Good. For the pilot, can we scope a 3-month POC with a small set of accounts to prove ROI?
[03:11] Elena Park: That's reasonable. Typical pilot is 6-12 weeks operational plus a short exec review. Success metrics — conversion lift, cost per query, and latency p95 — does that align?
[03:23] Tom Redding: p95 latency target needs to be under 300ms for certain payments use cases.
[03:29] Marcus Li: Understood, we'll validate that on our bench. If we can't hit it on hosted, we'll recommend Dedicated or edge routing.
[03:38] Carlos Mendez: Who owns the initial outreach? We'd like Verdant to run the first wave then Redwood joins on follow-ups.
[03:46] Elena Park: Fine. We'll provide messaging and joint decks for the emails. Elena to send templates.
[03:52] Priya Kaur: Also need a decision on deal crediting. Verdant needs primary sales credit for the first 12 months if we open.
[04:00] Elena Park: We'll draft a commercial proposal that covers crediting and revenue share and run it by legal.
[04:07] Tom Redding: My ask — executive alignment next week with Redwood head of sales. I can do 8/31 or 9/1.
[04:15] Elena Park: Let's tentatively book the week of 8/31; Elena to coordinate.
[04:20] 
[04:30] Marcus Li: Switching to technical details — for the bench we want an anonymized sample of typical chat transcripts and a small embedding corpus. We'll measure tokens-per-call, latency p50/p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens at projected volume.
[04:46] Lena Zhao: I can extract a 10k-turn sample and a 5k-document embed set. Expect some PII; we'll sanitize.
[04:55] Marcus Li: That's perfect. Also note our runtime picks optimized kernels depending on seq length distribution and the hardware — so share the length histogram if possible.
[05:08] Carlos Mendez: On the outreach play: Verdant will prioritize 8 accounts. We'll mark two as high-priority (closed-won potential this quarter), three medium, three long-term.
[05:20] Priya Kaur: I'll send the CSV of accounts and current stage; please keep that internal.
[05:27] Elena Park: We'll treat it as confidential. We'll also map decision-makers we should target.
[05:33] 
[05:45] Marcus Li: A small note — some of those customers have strict data residency. If they require EU-only hosting we'll recommend region pinning. There's a small perf delta but regulatory needs drive it.
[05:58] Tom Redding: We need to make sure the partner portal shows co-sell credits and pipeline visibility. Priya, can you use your CRM to push updates?
[06:08] Priya Kaur: yes, we can push weekly updates, but we need the integration setup. Does Redwood have a native SFDC connector?
[06:16] Elena Park: Yes, we have a connector and can set up weekly pipeline syncs. We'll share the connector doc and what fields to push.
[06:24] 
[06:40] Carlos Mendez: Competitor question — CloudGrid recently started a partner-backed offering; how is Redwood differentiated?
[06:47] Elena Park: Our edge is runtime performance + observability. We show token-level cost breakdowns, rollouts with automatic fallback, and a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private. Also we provide optimization recommendations — batching and quantization profiles — that often cut unit cost by 20–40%.
[07:08] Marcus Li: And from the SE side we help with kernel-level optimizations and recommend model variants per workload.
[07:15] 
[07:30] Priya Kaur: Ok, next steps recap?
[07:33] Elena Park: Recap: Elena will send co-sell one-pager, deck, intro email templates, and pricing scenarios. Marcus will set up bench and request data. Priya will share account list. Carlos will draft outreach sequence. We'll aim to have bench results and deck out before the week of 8/31 exec alignment.
[07:51] Tom Redding: That works. I need a short executive slide for my leadership — can we get an ROI slide?
[07:58] Elena Park: Yes, we'll include an ROI summary in the deck.
[08:04] 
[08:15] Lena Zhao: One more technical ask — we might want a small in-person workshop during the bench to tune model prompts. Is Redwood able to do a half-day prompt engineering session?
[08:24] Marcus Li: Absolutely, Marcus can lead a half-day remote workshop; in-person we can discuss later.
[08:30] Priya Kaur: Great.
[08:33] Elena Park: Any outstanding risks?
[08:36] Carlos Mendez: Main risk is price pushback from customers when we suggest Dedicated. Also timeline for private deploy can be 6–8 weeks which could slow pilots.
[08:46] Elena Park: We'll mark those as risks and propose mitigation — temporary hosted fallback and a phased Dedicated ramp.
[08:54] 
[09:05] Priya Kaur: ok if we get the docs by Monday we can draft outreach and land the exec alignment.
[09:11] Elena Park: We'll prioritize that.
[09:15] 
[09:40] Elena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow-up with the attachments and calendar invites.
[09:47] Tom Redding: Thanks, bye.
[09:50] Meeting ends.
